title: BIPM fixes the speed of light in vacuum at 299 792 458 m/s
summary: c is one of the seven defining constants. The value has no uncertainty. The metre depends on this number and on the second.
body: BIPM's defining-constants table gives the speed of light in vacuum, c, as 299 792 458 m s⁻¹, and says the seven defining values have no uncertainty. The NIST 2022 complete listing also prints 'speed of light in vacuum 299 792 458 (exact) m s⁻¹'. An exact mark means the number is defined, not a measurement that still carries a standard uncertainty in that table. The core pack already has a CODATA card for this value. This shard repeats the figure because an add-on pack has to stand on its own when it is the file a device just loaded.

sources.title: The International System of Units (SI): Defining constants
sources.author: Bureau International des Poids et Mesures
sources.note: Page opened 2026-11-18. BIPM dates the fixed values to the revision that took effect on 20 May 2019 and cites CGPM Resolution 1 (2018).
